title: Challenge of the Yukon
paragraphs: Northern adventure centered on Royal Canadian Mounted Police Sergeant William Preston and his dog Yukon King. The program began as a WXYZ regional serial/adventure, expanded to ABC in 1947, moved to Mutual in 1950, and was renamed Sergeant Preston of the Yukon in November 1951.

GRH documents the program through WXYZ local/regional era (February 3, 1938 to May 28, 1947) on [[org|org.a0d8a72797b5185f|WXYZ]], ABC network era (June 12, 1947 to December 30, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], Mutual Challenge of the Yukon era (January 2, 1950 to November 11, 1951) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Mutual Sergeant Preston era (November 13, 1951 to 1954) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Jay Michael (announcer on 310 recordings and performer on 190 recordings), Paul Sutton (performer on 356 recordings), George W. Trendle (producer on 320 recordings, creator on 312 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and executive producer on 1 recording), Fred Flowerday (director on 308 recordings and performer on 15 recordings), Fran Striker (editor on 129 recordings, writer on 51 recordings, performer on 6 recordings, and story editor on 1 recording), Charles D. Livingstone (performer on 154 recordings, director on 3 recordings, editor on 2 recordings, producer on 2 recordings, and writer on 1 recording), and Mildred Merrill (writer on 122 recordings and announcer on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.a0d8a72797b5185f|WXYZ]] (originated at station), [[org|org.4873e07a843601f0|Michigan Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Murder and violent crime, Gold mining and prospecting, Working dogs, Robbery and theft, Royal Canadian Mounted Police / Mounties, and Mining claims and property disputes.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Mountie and northern-frontier adventure in American popular radio, Breakfast-cereal sponsorship and youth premiums, and Sergeant Preston across the radio-to-television transition.
